# **CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._  The price performance of the precious metals was rather negative through the middle of the month of April. Platinum was the weakest of the four major metals, seeing selling pressure developing and falling back below $1,600. In contrast, palladium caught a bid and moved higher steadily towards an upside target of $700. Silver traded in a narrow range but gold was more excitable, showing both safe haven and risk-related aspects of its personality. Overall, though, it moved little and its overperformance compared to platinum was testament to weakness in the platinum market rather than to any strength in gold.  Gold and palladium saw futures investors adding to their long positions during the week to the 17th of April, if only cautiously. Platinum and silver saw investor interest on COMEX/NYMEX fall. Overall, positioning is restrained by recent standards, reflecting a lessening of appetite for these metals as their prices have failed to match expectations for their performance. Of the four main metals, palladium seems most likely to benefit if any upwards price rises can trigger short covering.  Gold and silver both saw gentle net selling from the ETFs as their prices failed to excite any interest, whether buying or selling. Platinum suffered some selling pressure as the price dropped below $1,600 per ounce while palladium saw some buying interest, driven by its relative price outperformance compared to the other three metals. **David Jollie david.jollie@mitprecious.com Tel: +44 20 7489 6767** **23 April 2012** ##### **New York:** 200 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10166 0130 Tel: +1 212 878 4122 ##### **London:** 4th Floor, St Martins Court, 10 Paternoster Row, London EC4M 7BB Tel: +44 20 7489 6767 ##### **Hong Kong:** Suite 1306, Two Exchange Square, 8 Connaught Place, Central, Hong Kong Tel: +852 2899 2026 ##### **Tokyo:** 2-1 Ohtemachi 1-Chome, Chiyoda-Ku, Tokyo 100 Tel: +81 33 285 3407 ##### **Singapore:** 80 Robinson Road, #15-02, Singapore, 068898 Tel: +65 6372 8050 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **23 April 2012** ### **Gold CFTC data to 17 April 2012; ETF data to 20 April 2012.** **Exchange (COMEX and TOCOM) and ETF Gold Investment (oz)** ||**COMEX**

Overall, it fell from $1,640 early on the 10th to its current sub-$1,630 levels despite heightened awareness of the European sovereign debt issues, triggered by Spanish ten year bond yields rising above six per cent, and the end of the Indian jewellers strike. The first sharp fall came on the 10th of April when gold dipped to $1,633 before bouncing to $1,660 in late US trading. On the 12th, gold drove higher again on its safe haven bid, rising to a peak of $1,680 before falling back. On the following day as poor Chinese growth figures were released and fears of a hard landing intensified. Gold settled at $1,650 for a few days before stepping down to $1,640 until the end of the week. Although gold’s price performance is at best neutral over that period, it did manage to outperform platinum and silver, suggesting that the safe haven aspect of its character was worth something to investors. #### **Gold Exchange Investment, Jan 10 — Apr12** 40 2,000 Gold price, $/oz

-  Derivatives investors increased their exposure to gold in the week to the 17th of April both on TOCOM and on COMEX. On TOCOM, net long speculative positioning climbed by 9,000 ounces to 1.58 million ounces: on COMEX it climbed by 305,000 ounces to 18.3 million ounces. For the moment, investors remain cautiously long overall but it seems that some external signal might be required in order to rekindle buying interest and send net positioning significantly higher. -  Gold ETF holdings changed little in the week to the 20th of April. With the price moving little, there was little incentive for ETF investors to buy or to sell. -  The gold:silver ratio has moved in gold’s favour throughout August even as the price of the yellow metal declined. News of production capacity cuts at one of the largest solar panel manufacturers reinforced the sense of relatively weak physical demand and with COMEX and ETF investors unable to take up the slack, the silver price has weakened from $33.20 on the 3rd of April to its current $30.60 per ounce. From the 10th onwards, though, there was little action with silver trading in a very narrow range from $31.25 to $32 almost throughout. The first exception was from the 12th to the 13th, when silver first bounced with gold in late New York trading as shortcovering was triggered and then fell back, along with gold, when weak Chinese economic data was released. This decline came despite the announcement of cuts in silver margins on COMEX, something that should have been bullish. The move lower on the 23rd was triggered again by poor Chinese economic data, suggesting that some investors at least are aware of silver’s partindustrial nature. -  Net long speculative positioning for silver on COMEX dropped by 1.3 million ounces in the week to 151 million ounces. It h

as fallen for six of the past seven weeks, shedding 106 million ounces in that time, demonstrating weak investor appetite for this metal. The silver price has fallen by over$5 per ounce during this period and, although it has stabilised somewhat, a stronger gold price may be needed to revive investor interest. -  Silver ETF positions declined for the fifth time in the last six weeks leading up to the 20th of April. As with gold, the selling pressure was only minor but positioning did drop by 1.3 million ounces to 454.3 million ounces. It has now fallen by 6.6 million ounces from its high for 2012, suggesting a degree of disinterest amongst investors. 3 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **23 April 2012** ### **Platinum CFTC data to 17 April 2012; ETF data to 20 April 2012.** ## **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Platinum Investment (oz)** ||**Nymex**

-  The platinum price disappointed throughout midApril, underperforming gold and moving into a roughly $70 discount to the yellow metal once again. Selling was seen on the 10th under a bout of risk aversion where gold benefited from its safe haven status but platinum did not. The price of the latter fell from $1,628 on the 10th to a low of $1,585. Platinum did bounce to $1,608 on the 13th but as the European crisis continued to rumble on it slipped back to a low of $1,562 on the 16th as it triggered some stop loss selling in Asia. Sentiment was by now rather muted and with little other excitement evident,

platinum settled close to $1,580 until the end of the week. It has since fallen below $1,550 on widespread weakness across the commodities markets. -  Investors are currently rather bearish towards platinum on a short term basis (although universally bullish over the longer term). Net long speculative NYMEX positions have now fallen for seven consecutive weeks, dropping from 1.68 million ounces to 1.09 million ounces. Although this does provide room for a move higher, most of this change has been due to long liquidation rather than the opening of new short positions, so the scope for a short covering rally is somewhat limited. -  Platinum ETF changes were bearish as the price fell below $1,600 with investors selling a net 16,300 ounces. Positions have fallen by 57,000 ounces since the start of March, to 1.46 million ounces despite some supply side issues in Southern Africa. 4 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **23 April 2012** ### **Palladium CFTC data to 17 April 2012; ETF data to 20 April 2012.** ## **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Palladium Investment (oz)** |**Date**|**Nymex**

Having fallen from a high of $725 at the end of February to a low of $630 on the 10th of April, palladium may have hit a short term low, finding support at that level and recovering to trade at $669 currently. The decrease of margins on NYMEX positions which was announced on the 12th of April may have encouraged some additional long investment to offset the general weakness seen in the precious metals market. -  Futures positioning in palladium was almost unchanged in the week to the 17th of April. However, this was hugely more positive than the four weeks of net selling which had preceded this, during which net long speculative positioning fell from 1.23 million ounces to 530,000 ounces, a low level by recent standards. Although short positioning continues to rise, additional long positions were opened. Combined short non-commercial and nonreportable positions are now at their highest since late November. -  Palladium’s outperformance in price terms prompted ETF bu

ying with investors buying for the fourth successive week. Although they added only 2,500 ounces in taking global holdings to 2.01 million ounces, net buying this year is already in excess of 270,000 ounces. #### **Palladium Exchange Investment, Jan 10 — Apr 12** 1,000
